subject: maths
question: While selling an item, a businessman allows a 40% discount on the marked price and incurs a loss of 30%. If the item is sold at the marked price, profit will be _______.
solution:
**Given:**

Discount Percentage = 40%

Loss Percentage = 30%

**Concept Used:**

Cost Price = (100)/(100-Loss\%)times SP

Profit % = (Profit)/(CP)times 100

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let the marked price be Rs 100

⇒ Selling price = 100 – 40% of 100

⇒ Selling price = 100-(40)/(100)times 100=100-40=60 Rs

⇒ Loss percentage = 30%

⇒ So, Cost price = (100)/(100-30)times 60

⇒ Cost price = (100)/(70)times 60=(600)/(7) Rs

⇒ If item is sold at marked price, then

⇒ Profit Percentage = (100-frac{600)/(7)}{(600)/(7)}times 100

⇒ Profit Percentage = (frac{700-600)/(7)}{(600)/(7)}times 100=(100)/(600)times 100=(100)/(6)=16(2)/(3) %

**Hence, the profit percentage made by selling an item at marked price is 16(2)/(3)\%**.
